pos.personaBrief: Catenaccio gave up territory and possession for solidity and used counter-attacking as the natural attacking method (Guide to Football, verified); Inter and Milan won the ball back and launched quick counters.

pro.personaBrief: Herrera and Rocco both wanted direct vertical passes and rejected horizontal football as a waste of time; counters were quick and precise, with long balls to relieve pressure.

est.personaBrief: A fixed libero behind tight markers with assigned duties and a strict regime points to defined roles and a rigid structure, not fluid rondo-style combinations; vertical passing meant few close one-twos.

lar.personaBrief: Attacks ran through a central playmaker (Suarez, Rivera) with vertical balls, while Facchetti's overlapping full-back runs gave the flank outlet; no wingers-and-crosses ideology.

blo.personaBrief: Deep defence with a libero, five players with no attacking duties, and Inter dropping everyone behind the ball once ahead; the team waited rather than pressed.

mar.personaBrief: Core of the system: each defender man-marks one attacker and follows him everywhere, with a free libero sweeping; Herrera had Burgnich mark Johnstone and Rocco ordered marking from the dressing room to the toilet.

pla.personaBrief: Rocco studied every opponent in detail and Herrera assigned markers to the danger man, but the system was also a fixed model imposed with a strict regime; it was the weak-side tool to neutralise stronger teams.

res.personaBrief: Result above all: Inter pulled everyone behind the ball with a lead, the system was the 'right of the weak', and Rocco replied 'I hope not' to 'may the best team win'.

sis.personaBrief: The system and its roles were central (libero as extension of the coach, strict duties); stars were integrated into the collective and expected to work.

jog.personaBrief: Brera argued Italians had to adapt to the physicality of others; Rocco demanded extreme fitness and tracking, Herrera heavy training; yet playmakers like Suarez and Rivera had a place.

bas.personaBrief: Herrera signed Picchi and Suarez and Rocco built around seasoned players; the focus was winning titles with a drilled group, not academy development.

lid.personaBrief: Herrera was a strict disciplinarian who checked players' homes and banned smoking and drinking; Rocco berated referees and humiliated young players; coach decided alone.
